airport.name: Denpasar I Gusti Ngurah Rai International Airport

summary: Denpasar I Gusti Ngurah Rai International Airport is Bali's primary international gateway, located in Tuban near the popular beach resort area of Kuta. Named after I Gusti Ngurah Rai, a Balinese national hero who died in the 1946 Battle of Margarana, the airport serves as the main entry point for millions of tourists visiting the island each year. It features separate domestic and international terminals and operates as a key hub connecting Bali to destinations across Southeast Asia, Australia, and beyond.
faqs:
Q: How far is the airport from Kuta and Seminyak?
A: The airport is adjacent to Kuta, just a few minutes' drive, and approximately 20-30 minutes by car to Seminyak depending on traffic.

Q: Are there currency exchange and ATM facilities at DPS?
A: Yes, the airport has multiple ATMs and currency exchange counters in both international and domestic terminals, though rates outside the airport are generally more favorable.

Q: Does the airport have free Wi-Fi?
A: Yes, complimentary Wi-Fi is available throughout the terminals, though many travelers find local SIM cards or eSIMs more reliable for longer stays.

Q: Is there a duty-free shop at DPS?
A: Yes, there are duty-free shops in the international departure area offering liquor, tobacco, cosmetics, and local goods.
transport_tips: Official taxi counters inside the arrivals hall offer fixed-rate vouchers to popular destinations, which helps avoid overcharging. Ride-hailing apps like Grab and Gojek operate at designated pick-up zones outside the terminal. Pre-booked private transfers are widely available and recommended during peak arrival hours when traffic around Kuta can be heavy.
local_tip: For a smoother exit during peak season, walk to the far end of the airport area or the adjacent shopping plaza to catch a ride-hailing car, as the main pick-up zones can have long queues and the walkways from the terminal are only a few minutes longer.
